#LIM set up and validity of the solution
```{r}
############################ 2009 ##########################
# File path for 2009 data
abrilfw09 <- "Input_files_LIM/FW_2009_bact.txt"
abrilfw12 <- "Input_files_LIM/FW_2012_bact.txt"
abrilfw16 <- "Input_files_LIM/FW_2016_bact.txt"
abrilfw19 <- "Input_files_LIM/FW_2019_bact.txt"
abrilfw22 <- "Input_files_LIM/FW_2022_bact.txt"

# Read data
readLIM.abril09 <- LIM::Read(file = abrilfw09, verbose = TRUE, checkLinear = TRUE)
readLIM.abril12 <- LIM::Read(file = abrilfw12, verbose = TRUE, checkLinear = TRUE)
readLIM.abril16 <- LIM::Read(file = abrilfw16, verbose = TRUE, checkLinear = TRUE)
readLIM.abril19 <- LIM::Read(file = abrilfw19, verbose = TRUE, checkLinear = TRUE)
readLIM.abril22 <- LIM::Read(file = abrilfw22, verbose = TRUE, checkLinear = TRUE)


LIM.abril09 <- Setup(readLIM.abril09)
LIM.abril12 <- Setup(readLIM.abril12)
LIM.abril16 <- Setup(readLIM.abril16)
LIM.abril19 <- Setup(readLIM.abril19)
LIM.abril22 <- Setup(readLIM.abril22)

# Calculate solution and check validity of the solution
Solldeiabril09 <- Ldei(LIM.abril09, verbose = TRUE)
#Rangesabril09 <- lim.ranges(LIM.abril09)
any((LIM.abril09$A %*% Solldeiabril09$X - LIM.abril09$B) > 1e-8)
any((LIM.abril09$G %*% Solldeiabril09$X - LIM.abril09$H) < (-1e-8))

Solldeiabril12 <- Ldei(LIM.abril12, verbose = TRUE)
#Rangesabril12 <- lim.ranges(LIM.abril12)
any((LIM.abril12$A %*% Solldeiabril12$X - LIM.abril12$B) > 1e-8)
any((LIM.abril12$G %*% Solldeiabril12$X - LIM.abril12$H) < (-1e-8))

Solldeiabril16 <- Ldei(LIM.abril16, verbose = TRUE)
#Rangesabril16 <- lim.ranges(LIM.abril16)
any((LIM.abril16$A %*% Solldeiabril16$X - LIM.abril16$B) > 1e-8)
any((LIM.abril16$G %*% Solldeiabril16$X - LIM.abril16$H) < (-1e-8))

Solldeiabril19 <- Ldei(LIM.abril19, verbose = TRUE)
#Rangesabril19 <- lim.ranges(LIM.abril19)
any((LIM.abril19$A %*% Solldeiabril19$X - LIM.abril19$B) > 1e-8)
any((LIM.abril19$G %*% Solldeiabril19$X - LIM.abril19$H) < (-1e-8))

Solldeiabril22 <- Ldei(LIM.abril22, verbose = TRUE)
#Rangesabril22 <- lim.ranges(LIM.abril22)
any((LIM.abril22$A %*% Solldeiabril22$X - LIM.abril22$B) > 1e-8)
any((LIM.abril22$G %*% Solldeiabril22$X - LIM.abril22$H) < (-1e-8))

# Plot web diagram, change according to the year you want to plot
diagram::plotweb(Flowmatrix(lim = LIM.abril19, web = Solldeiabril19$X + 1),
  bty = "n", lab.size = 0.6, log = TRUE, leg.title = "log + 1"
)

```

```{r}
#Amount of carbon exported

# Step 1: Calculate total export per year
export_stats <- all_flow_stats %>%
  # Keep only flows going to EXP
  filter(grepl("EXP$", Flow)) %>%
  group_by(food_web_year) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_export = sum(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_export   = sqrt(sum(sd^2, na.rm = TRUE)),  # assuming independence
    min_export  = sum(min, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_export  = sum(max, na.rm = TRUE),
    lci_export  = sum(ci_lower, na.rm = TRUE),
    uci_export  = sum(ci_upper, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Step 2: Calculate total flow per year
total_flow <- all_flow_stats %>%
  group_by(food_web_year) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_total = sum(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_total   = sqrt(sum(sd^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    min_total  = sum(min, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_total  = sum(max, na.rm = TRUE),
    lci_total  = sum(ci_lower, na.rm = TRUE),
    uci_total  = sum(ci_upper, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Step 3: Combine and calculate percentage exported
export_summary <- export_stats %>%
  left_join(total_flow, by = "food_web_year") %>%
  mutate(
    percent_export_mean = (mean_export / mean_total) * 100,
    percent_export_lci  = (lci_export  / uci_total) * 100,
    percent_export_uci  = (uci_export  / lci_total) * 100
  )

# View the result
export_summary
```


#Calculate the variables for each repetition

**Resp:** Value of the flow going to DIC **Uptake:** All flows going to that compartment **Assimilation:** Uptake minus the flows going to detritus.
**Production:** Assimilation minus respiration

```{r, echo = F, fig.width=13, fig.height=10, include = F}

# -----------------------------
# 2009
# -----------------------------
Var_2009 <- matrix(NA, 
                   nrow = LIM.abril09$NVariables,
                   ncol = nrow(results_2009),
                   dimnames = list(LIM.abril09$Variables, 1:nrow(results_2009)))

for (i in 1:nrow(results_2009)) {
    Var_2009[, i] <- Variables(LIM.abril09, results_2009[i, ])$values
}

results_2009_stats <- data.frame(
    variable = LIM.abril09$Variables,
  mean     = round(apply(Var_2009, 1, mean, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
  sd       = round(apply(Var_2009, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
```

#Production and flows plot
```{r}
# =============================
# Prepare turbine variables plot ----
# =============================

selected_variables <- c("FlowsTOTR", "FlowsFROMTR", "ProdTURBINEROCK", "SeconProd", 
                        "TurbineTotal", "TotalRESP", "TotalUpta", "UptaTURBINEROCK")

extract_year_stats <- function(stats, year) {
  # Filter only the selected variables
  df <- stats %>% filter(variable %in% selected_variables)
  
  # Keep only the columns you want for plotting
  df <- df %>% select(variable, mean, sd, min, max, ci_lower, ci_upper)
  
  # Add the year
  df$year <- year
  
  df
}

combined_data <- bind_rows(
  extract_year_stats(results_2009_stats, 2009),
  extract_year_stats(results_2012_stats, 2012),
  extract_year_stats(results_2016_stats, 2016),
  extract_year_stats(results_2019_stats, 2019),
  extract_year_stats(results_2022_stats, 2022)
)

combined_data$variable <- factor(combined_data$variable, levels = selected_variables)

# Define patterns to exclude flows we don’t want in totals
exclude_patterns <- c("->DIC", "->EXP", "->BUR", "DIC->PHY", "EXP->", "BUR->", "DIC->")

# Filter out unwanted flows
filtered_2009 <- results_2009[, !grepl(paste(exclude_patterns, collapse = "|"), colnames(results_2009))]
filtered_2012 <- results_2012[, !grepl(paste(exclude_patterns, collapse = "|"), colnames(results_2012))]
filtered_2016 <- results_2016[, !grepl(paste(exclude_patterns, collapse = "|"), colnames(results_2016))]
filtered_2019 <- results_2019[, !grepl(paste(exclude_patterns, collapse = "|"), colnames(results_2019))]
filtered_2022 <- results_2022[, !grepl(paste(exclude_patterns, collapse = "|"), colnames(results_2022))]

# Compute row sums for each year
total_2009 <- rowSums(filtered_2009)
total_2012 <- rowSums(filtered_2012)
total_2016 <- rowSums(filtered_2016)
total_2019 <- rowSums(filtered_2019)
total_2022 <- rowSums(filtered_2022)

# Make a function to summarize
summarize_total_flow <- function(x, year, var_name) {
  data.frame(
    mean     = mean(x),
    sd       = sd(x),
    min      = min(x),
    max      = max(x),
    ci_lower = quantile(x, 0.025),
    ci_upper = quantile(x, 0.975),
    year     = year,
    variable = var_name
  )
}

# Apply to each year
total_flows_stats <- bind_rows(
  summarize_total_flow(total_2009, 2009, "Total Flows"),
  summarize_total_flow(total_2012, 2012, "Total Flows"),
  summarize_total_flow(total_2016, 2016, "Total Flows"),
  summarize_total_flow(total_2019, 2019, "Total Flows"),
  summarize_total_flow(total_2022, 2022, "Total Flows")
)

# Extract turbine flows from combined_data (calculated in earlier section)
flows_to_turbine <- combined_data %>% filter(variable == "TurbineTotal")

# Calculate non-turbine internal flows
non_turbine_flows_stats <- total_flows_stats
non_turbine_flows_stats$mean <- total_flows_stats$mean - flows_to_turbine$mean
non_turbine_flows_stats$variable <- "Non-Turbine Flows"

# Combine for plotting
combined_plot_data <- bind_rows(non_turbine_flows_stats, flows_to_turbine)

# Set factor levels to control stacking
combined_plot_data$variable <- factor(combined_plot_data$variable, levels = c("Non-Turbine Flows", "TurbineTotal"))

# Calculate % contribution of turbine flows
flows_to_turbine$percentage <- (flows_to_turbine$mean / total_flows_stats$mean) * 100
combined_plot_data$label <- ifelse(combined_plot_data$variable == "TurbineTotal",
                                   paste0(round(flows_to_turbine$percentage, 1), "%"),
                                   "")

# Format
combined_plot_data$year <- factor(combined_plot_data$year)
combined_plot_data$variable <- factor(combined_plot_data$variable, levels = c("Non-Turbine Flows","TurbineTotal"))

# Plot
col_palette <- c("Non-Turbine Flows" = "#377EB8", "TurbineTotal" = "#FF7F00")

turbine_variables_plot <- ggplot(combined_plot_data, aes(x = year, y = mean, fill = variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), color = "black") +
  geom_text(data = combined_plot_data %>% filter(variable == "TurbineTotal"),
            aes(label = label, y = mean + sd + 8),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold", hjust = -0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_palette,
                    labels = c("TurbineTotal" = "Hard-substrate fauna flows",
                               "Non-Turbine Flows" = "Internal flows")) +
  labs(title = expression("Internal flows and flows to hard-substrate community"),
       x = "Year",
       y = expression("Mean carbon flows (mmol C / m"^2*"/day)"),
       fill = "Flow Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.position = "bottom")


# =============================
# Prepare production plot ----
# =============================

prod_vars <- c("SeconProd", "ProdTURBINEROCK")

extract_prod_stats <- function(stats, year) {
  df <- stats %>% 
    filter(variable %in% prod_vars) %>% 
    select(variable, mean, sd, min, max, ci_lower, ci_upper) %>% 
    mutate(year = year)
  df
}

prod_data <- bind_rows(
  extract_prod_stats(results_2009_stats, 2009),
  extract_prod_stats(results_2012_stats, 2012),
  extract_prod_stats(results_2016_stats, 2016),
  extract_prod_stats(results_2019_stats, 2019),
  extract_prod_stats(results_2022_stats, 2022)
)

# Rename variables
prod_data$variable <- as.character(prod_data$variable)
prod_data$variable[prod_data$variable == "SeconProd"] <- "Secondary Production"
prod_data$variable[prod_data$variable == "ProdTURBINEROCK"] <- "Hard-substrate fauna production"
prod_data$variable <- factor(prod_data$variable, levels = c("Hard-substrate fauna production", "Secondary Production"))

# Calculate remaining secondary production
turbo <- prod_data %>% filter(variable == "Hard-substrate fauna production")
sec <- prod_data %>% filter(variable == "Secondary Production")

remaining_sec <- sec
remaining_sec$mean <- sec$mean - turbo$mean
remaining_sec$sd <- sqrt(sec$sd^2 + turbo$sd^2)
remaining_sec$variable <- "Remaining secondary production"

# Combine and recode factor levels
combined_prod <- bind_rows(turbo, remaining_sec)
#combined_prod$variable <- factor(combined_prod$variable,
 #                                levels = c("Remaining Secondary Production", "Hard-substrate production"))

# Calculate turbine % and labels
combined_prod <- combined_prod %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(mean),
         percentage = if_else(variable == "Hard-substrate fauna production", mean / total * 100, NA_real_),
         label = if_else(!is.na(percentage), paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%"), "")
  )

combined_prod$variable <- factor(combined_prod$variable,
                                 levels = c("Remaining secondary production", "Hard-substrate fauna production"))


# Production plot
col_palette_prod <- c(                      "Remaining secondary production" = "#4DAF4A",
                                            "Hard-substrate fauna production" = "#FF7F00" 
)

production_plot <- ggplot(combined_prod, aes(x = factor(year), y = mean, fill = variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
                width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_text(
    data = combined_prod %>% filter(variable == "Hard-substrate fauna production"),
    aes(label = label, y = mean + sd + 0.7),
    position = position_dodge(0.8),
    size = 4, fontface = "bold", hjust = -0.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_palette_prod) +
  labs(
    title = "Secondary and hard-substrate fauna production",
    x = "Year",
    y = expression("Mean production (mmol C / m"^2*"/day)"),
    fill = "Production Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

#General second production plots
```{r}

selected_variables <- c("ProdFISH", "ProdSED", "ProdTURBINEROCK", "ProdUBIQUOUS")

extract_year_stats <- function(stats, year) {
  df <- stats[selected_variables, ]
  colnames(df) <- c("mean", "sd")
  df$year <- year
  df$variable <- rownames(df)
  df
}


combined_data <- bind_rows(
  extract_year_stats(results_2009_stats, 2009),
  extract_year_stats(results_2012_stats, 2012),
  extract_year_stats(results_2016_stats, 2016),
  extract_year_stats(results_2019_stats, 2019),
  extract_year_stats(results_2022_stats, 2022)
)

combined_data$year <- factor(combined_data$year)

plot_production_variable <- function(data, var_name, fill_color = "#377EB8") {
  # Define descriptive titles for each variable
  title_map <- c(
    "ProdFISH"      = "Secondary Production Fish",
    "ProdSED"       = "Secondary Production Sediment",
    "ProdTURBINEROCK"   = "Secondary Production Hard-substrate",
    "ProdUBIQUOUS"  = "Secondary Production Ubiquitous"
  )

  # Extract correct data and title
  plot_data <- data %>% filter(variable == var_name)
  plot_title <- title_map[[var_name]]

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = year, y = mean)) +
    geom_col(fill = fill_color, width = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
                  width = 0.2, color = "black") +
    labs(title = plot_title,
         x = "Year",
         y = expression("Production (mmol C " * m^{-2} * " day"^{-1} * ")")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
}

plot_prodFISH     <- plot_production_variable(combined_data, "ProdFISH")
plot_prodSED      <- plot_production_variable(combined_data, "ProdSED")
plot_prodTURBINE  <- plot_production_variable(combined_data, "ProdTURBINEROCK")
plot_prodUBIQUOUS <- plot_production_variable(combined_data, "ProdUBIQUOUS")


Production = plot_prodFISH + plot_prodSED + plot_prodTURBINE + plot_prodUBIQUOUS +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)

ggsave("~/phD/WP1_TemporalFW/manuscript/Figures/Production_suppl.png", Production, height = 12, width = 12)
```

#Credible intervals of network indices
```{r}

PathIndices_all$Network = as.numeric(PathIndices_all$Network)
PathIndices_all <- PathIndices_all %>%
  mutate(
    TSTC = as.numeric(TSTC),
    TSTS = as.numeric(TSTS),
    FCI = as.numeric(FCI),
    FCIb = as.numeric(FCIb),
    APL  = as.numeric(APL)
  )

CI_table_path <- PathIndices_all %>%
  group_by(Network) %>%
  summarise(
    median_FCIb = median(FCIb),
            sd_FCIb     = sd(FCIb, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_FCIb = min(FCIb),
    max_FCIb= max(FCIb),
    CI_low_FCIb = quantile(FCIb, 0.025),
    CI_high_FCIb = quantile(FCIb, 0.975),
  )

GenIndices_all$Network = as.numeric(GenIndices_all$Network)
GenIndices_all <- GenIndices_all %>%
  mutate(
    T.. = as.numeric(`T..`),
    TST = as.numeric(TST),
    Lint = as.numeric(Lint),
    Ltot = as.numeric(Ltot),
    LD = as.numeric(LD),
    C = as.numeric(C),
    Tijbar = as.numeric(Tijbar),
    TSTbar = as.numeric(TSTbar),
    Cbar = as.numeric(Cbar)
  )

CI_table_Gen <- GenIndices_all %>%

  )

        min_T = min(`ACratio`),
    max_T= max(ACratio),
    CI_low_T   = quantile(`ACratio`, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    CI_high_T  = quantile(`ACratio`, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
  )

write.csv(CI_table_path, "~/phD/WP1_TemporalFW/LIM/PathIndices2_CI_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#Statistical comparison of years
```{r}

library(car)

GenIndices_all$T.. = as.numeric(GenIndices_all$T..)

# 1. Shapiro-Wilk test for normality in each year
shapiro_results <- GenIndices_all %>%
  group_by(Network) %>%
  summarise(
    W = shapiro.test(T..)$statistic,
    p_value = shapiro.test(T..)$p.value
  )

print("Shapiro-Wilk normality test per group:")
print(shapiro_results)

# 2. Levene's test for equal variances
print("Levene’s test for homogeneity of variances:")
levene_result <- leveneTest(T.. ~ Network, data = GenIndices_all)
print(levene_result)

# 3. Diagnostic plot (Q-Q)
ggplot(GenIndices_all, aes(sample = T..)) +
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line() + 
  facet_wrap(~ Network) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Q-Q plots for normality check")


# Kruskal–Wallis test
kruskal_test <- kruskal.test(T.. ~ Network, data = GenIndices_all)
print(kruskal_test)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon test with Holm correction
pairwise_wilcox <- pairwise.wilcox.test(GenIndices_all$`T..`, GenIndices_all$Network, 
                                        p.adjust.method = "holm")

print(pairwise_wilcox)

PathIndices_all$FCIb = as.numeric(PathIndices_all$FCIb)

# Kruskal–Wallis test
kruskal_test <- kruskal.test(FCIb ~ Network, data = PathIndices_all)
print(kruskal_test)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon test with Holm correction
pairwise_wilcox <- pairwise.wilcox.test(PathIndices_all$FCIb, PathIndices_all$Network, 
                                        p.adjust.method = "holm")

print(pairwise_wilcox)

link_weights_all$Variance_Link_Weight = as.numeric(link_weights_all$Variance_Link_Weight)

# Kruskal–Wallis test
kruskal_test <- kruskal.test(Variance_Link_Weight ~ Network, data = link_weights_all)
print(kruskal_test)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon test with Holm correction
pairwise_wilcox <- pairwise.wilcox.test(link_weights_all$Variance_Link_Weight, link_weights_all$Network, 
                                        p.adjust.method = "holm")

print(pairwise_wilcox)

AscIndices_all$ACratio = as.numeric(AscIndices_all$ACratio )

# 1. Shapiro-Wilk test for normality in each year
shapiro_results <- AscIndices_all %>%
  group_by(Network) %>%
  summarise(
    W = shapiro.test(ACratio)$statistic,
    p_value = shapiro.test(ACratio)$p.value
  )

print("Shapiro-Wilk normality test per group:")
print(shapiro_results)

# 2. Levene's test for equal variances
print("Levene’s test for homogeneity of variances:")
levene_result <- leveneTest(ACratio ~ Network, data = AscIndices_all)
print(levene_result)

# 3. Diagnostic plot (Q-Q)
ggplot(AscIndices_all, aes(sample = ACratio)) +
  stat_qq() + 
  stat_qq_line() + 
  facet_wrap(~ Network) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Q-Q plots for normality check")


# Kruskal–Wallis test
kruskal_test <- kruskal.test(ACratio ~ Network, data = AscIndices_all)
print(kruskal_test)

# Pairwise Wilcoxon test with Holm correction
pairwise_wilcox <- pairwise.wilcox.test(AscIndices_all$`ACratio`, AscIndices_all$Network,
```

```{r}
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = "E", hjust = -0.5, vjust = 1.5, size = 6, fontface = "bold")

# Arrange the plots
first_plot <- (GenPlot_with_CI | PathPlot_with_CI | ascendency_IS) + 
  plot_layout(ncol = 3, heights = c(1))

second_plot <- (production_plot + turbine_variables_plot) + 
  plot_layout(ncol = 2, heights = c(1))

final_plot <- first_plot / second_plot + 
  plot_layout(ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 1))

# Save the final plot
ggsave("~/phD/WP1_TemporalFW/manuscript/Figures/ENA_indices.tif", plot = final_plot, dpi = 300, width = 13, height = 9)
```

### Sample diagnostics

There are two types of diagnostics:
- Plots: you visualize how good the sampling space is sampled
- Diagnostic: are used to asses statistical convergence. 

A lot of those plots and diagnostics are done at the level of flows, therefore, we have around 500 plots to visually check, therefore, sometimes diagnostics are more easy.

1. Check sample coverage and whether jumpsize is ok

**The Raftery and Lewis diagnostic**

The main principle behind the Raftery and Lewis diagnostic is that a correct sample of the objective distribution, here the uniform distribution, should give precise estimates of its quantiles. Usually the 0.025 quantile is used.

This diagnostic provides multiple pieces of information, such as the burning value (M), an estimate of the sample size to ensure precise estimation of a prescribed quantile (N), a lower bound (Nmin), and a dependence factor (I).

The dependence factor assesses the extent to which auto-correlation inflates the required sample size; values larger than 5 indicate a strong auto-correlation.

```{r}
q <- 0.025
RL <- coda::raftery.diag(data = results_2012, q=q)
RL
```

**The Geweke diagnostic**

The Geweke diagnostic is a classical statistical test of comparison of means applied to prescribed proportions of the first and last points generated by an MCMC algorithm. For each variable, a value $Z$ is computed, the hypothesis of convergence of the algorithm is rejected if $\left| Z \right|$ exceeds a prescribed quantile of the normal distribution. With $p_1 = 0.1$ and $p_2 = 0.5$, convergence is rejected when $\left| Z \right| \geq 1.28$.  f the flow has reached stationarity, the means of the two parts
will be equal (Plummer et al., 2020), reflected by a Geweke Z-score
between −1.96 and 1.96 (corresponding to p = 0.05).

Evaluates stationarity, values should be between -1.96 and 1.96

```{r}
frac1 <- 0.1
frac2 <- 0.5
G <- coda::geweke.diag(results_2009, frac1 = frac1, frac2 = frac2)
G

# Subset flows where Z < -1.96 or Z > 1.96
flows_outside_1.96 <- G$z[G$z < -1.28 | G$z > 1.28]

# Visualize the subset
print(flows_outside_1.96)
```

**Heidelberger and Welch's convergence diagnostic**
Determines the stationary of the variables in the MCMC chain and burn-in periods.
It first tests the stationary of the sample chain and he second (halfwidth test) tests if there are enough samples to estimate the mean of the flow values with an acceptable degree of precision.

```{r}
coda::heidel.diag(results_2009)
```

**Effective Sample Size**

The Effective Sample Size (ESS) reflects the amount of autocorrelation in the MCMC draws. The closer ESS is to N (the sample size), the better, since it means that the draws are lowly auto-correlated.
ESS > 10% of total iterations

```{r}

#Get total number of iterations
total_iters <- nrow(results_2009[[1]])

#Get effective sample sizes
ess <- coda::effectiveSize(results_2009)

#Identify flows with ESS < 10% of total iterations
low_ess_flows <- ess[ess < 0.1 * total_iters]

print(low_ess_flows)

```

**Kernel density plots**
Shows the sample PDF p(x) where stationarity can be iferrred if P(x) approaches the underlying soluton space of PDF q(x). You expect a gaussian disttribution if the flow is properly sampled.

**Trace plot and autocorrelation plots**
Shows the mixing and autocorelation plots. You expect a catepillat for a well sampled flow.  Trace plots show the
sampled value of a flow at each iteration of the MCMC chain. A well- sampled flow looks like a ’hairy caterpillar’ (Roy, 2020) i.e., a visually random pattern that indicates good mixing (van den Meersche et al., 2009) (Fig. 4 H).

Autocorrelation plots indicate correlation between successive solutions and, therefore, the proportion of samples that can be considered ‘independent’(Hogg and Foreman-Mackey, 2018). Specifically, the plots show the lag-k (sample) autocorrelation between k steps apart (Roy, 2020). For fast mixing MCMC chains, lag-k autocorrelation values drop to zero almost as quickly as k increases (Roy, 2020) (Fig. 4 I).

*Run mean plots* 
Test the sample efficiency. If it does not stabilize at a fixed value, then more iterations are needed.

```{r}
results = as.data.frame(results_2016)
mcmc_plots(results,flow = "JASSATR->SPOM")
```

#Check the convergence of the results
```{r}
## Convergence
## convergence function

 convergence <- function(Bay  = NULL,
                         stp  = NULL,
                         flow = flow)
  {                       
  sdevs <- vector("numeric",stp)
  means <- vector("numeric",stp)
  n     <- nrow(Bay)
  for (i in 1:stp){
    random   <-sort(runif(n),index.return=TRUE) 
    sdevs[i] <-   sd(Bay[random$ix[1:(i*(n/stp))],flow])
    means[i] <- mean(Bay[random$ix[1:(i*(n/stp))],flow])
    }
  plot(seq(from=n/stp,n,by=n/stp),means,xlab="No of solutions",ylab="flow value",main=colnames(Bay)[flow],sub="mean")
  plot(seq(from=n/stp,n,by=n/stp),sdevs,xlab="No of solutions",ylab="flow value",main=colnames(Bay)[flow],sub="st. devs")
  
  return(cbind(means, sdevs))
  
 }

 par(mfrow=c(2,2))
 stp   <- 1000  #step with increase of solutions
 flow <- which(colnames(results_2009)==names(sort(colMaxs(results_2009),decreasing = TRUE)[1]))
 result_maxflow <- convergence(Bay=results_2009, stp= 1000 ,flow=flow)
 flow  <- which(colnames(results_2009)==names(sort(colMins(results_2009)[which(colMins(results_2009)>0)],decreasing = FALSE)[1]))
 result_minflow <- convergence(Bay=results_2009, stp= 1000 ,flow=flow)
 var(result_maxflow[2:50,"sdevs"])
var(result_maxflow[2:1000,"sdevs"])
 var(result_maxflow[2:1000,"sdevs"])/var(result_maxflow[2:50,"sdevs"])*100
var(result_minflow[2:50,"sdevs"])
 var(result_minflow[2:1000,"sdevs"])
 var(result_minflow[2:1000,"sdevs"])/var(result_minflow[2:50,"sdevs"])*100
 
  par(mfrow=c(2,2))

 flow  <- which(colnames(results_2012)==names(sort(colMins(results_2012)[which(colMins(results_2012)>0)],decreasing = FALSE)[1]))
 result_minflow <- convergence(Bay=results_2012, stp= 1000 ,flow=flow)
```
